summary: Beyond the Forecast is a ground-truthing web dashboard that compares regional satellite data with the real microclimates people feel on the ground. For the Be an Earth System Trend Detective challenge, I built a virtual telemetry node that logs temperature and humidity across four everyday environments and cross-references them against a NASA Worldview baseline. Direct sunlight ran significantly hotter than the regional satellite average, proving microclimate heating. Because single regional averages hide these dangerous local heat spikes, ground-truthing is essential for protecting public health and improving urban planning.
details: Beyond the Forecast is a ground-truthing web dashboard that compares regional satellite data with what people actually feel on the ground. Because satellites like Terra/MODIS measure broad 1 km grid cells, they miss the sharp heat differences people experience in daily life. Using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on CodePen with browser LocalStorage, I built a virtual telemetry node that simulates a DHT11 sensor and serial monitor across four everyday settings in Bahrain: direct sunlight, shade, an uncooled room, and an AC room. Users log readings and enter a baseline from NASA Worldview (using the September 23, 2026 Land Surface Temperature layer over Aali) to calculate the exact temperature offset. I specifically calibrated this prototype for September 23 conditions so the simulation stays scientifically honest while proving how low-cost sensors can support public health, urban shade planning, and citizen science.
